title: Paloma and the Uniform
premise: In the winter of a nation's civil war, Astrid Quintana keeps the light at Paloma Point with her late husband's niece, Sef, and an old keeper's uniform that belonged to Astrid's father—a man who served the losing side. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Quintanas as heirs to documents proving a massacre was ordered, not accidental, Astrid must choose between burning the letter and carrying it upriver to the provisional capital before the ice breaks and the victors' historians seal the record. Pursued by a former comrade of her father who wants the papers destroyed, Astrid and Sef make the journey, discovering along the way that the family they've been keeping alive is the family they already are. The book ends with Astrid testifying her truth into the record as the river thaws, then returning to relight the lamp—no longer invisible, but no longer alone.
about_author: Kestrel Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from forgotten wars before turning to fiction. They live near a working lighthouse and write about the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Light Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Establishes the rhythm of the light, Sef's restless grief, and Astrid's creed that history happens elsewhere. A supply boat brings news of the war advancing downriver; Astrid logs it and moves on. Emotional beat: the comfort—and cost—of deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed Twice
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The supply boat leaves behind a sealed letter addressed to 'the Quintana family,' in her dead uncle's hand. Sef hides it from Astrid for three days, reading it by lamplight: it names a hidden archive and a massacre. Emotional beat: the vertigo of inheriting someone else's guilt.

chapters.title: What Father Wore
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Confronted, Astrid finally tells Sef about her father—the uniformed officer whose side lost, whose silence she inherited like the coat itself. She burns nothing but can't yet decide anything. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited identity, worn like wool.

chapters.title: The Man from the Old Regiment
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A stranger arrives asking quiet questions about Quintana papers—an old comrade of Astrid's father, courteous and cold. He leaves a warning wrapped in hospitality. Emotional beat: the first true fear; invisibility failing as armor.

chapters.title: Ice on the River, Ink on the Page
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef finds the archive cache in the boathouse: affidavits, a muster list, her uncle's confession. Astrid begins copying everything in duplicate. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing—grief converted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Choice at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The stranger returns with an offer: burn it all, keep the light, keep Sef safe. Astrid nearly accepts. That night she dresses in her father's uniform and understands she cannot pass his silence to another generation. Emotional beat: the hinge of the book—choosing witness over safety.

chapters.title: Upriver Before the Break
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The two travel upriver by sledge and borrowed skiff, dodging patrols, carrying duplicates sewn into their coats. A checkpoint scene forces Sef to lie fluently for the first time. Emotional beat: found family tested under pressure and holding.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Truth
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The comrade intercepts them—not to kill them, but to confess: he ordered the cover-up and has been dying of it. He gives Astrid his own testimony rather than take hers. Emotional beat: enemy becoming evidence; mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. In the capital, amid victors drafting their histories, Astrid files the affidavits and speaks her testimony while the ice groans on the river below the window. Officials resist; a young clerk quietly enters it anyway. Emotional beat: climax—truth entering the official record against the current.

chapters.title: Paloma, Relit
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Spring. The river runs free; word comes that the testimony will be read into the national archive. Astrid and Sef climb the tower together to light the lamp, the uniform now folded in a chest, not worn as a burden. Emotional beat: resolution—visible at last, and home.
